items.title: Iranian woman moves Madras High Court wanting to know procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous visa
points: Pegah Ansari, daughter of Ansari Shapour, told the court that she was born and raised in a Zoroastrian family in Tehran.
Her second stop was Sri Lanka where stayed approximately for a month before flying down to India on a one-month-long tourist visa in April 2022.

“I came to India in search of safety, stability, and the freedom to live without fear of religious persecution,” the petitioner said and claimed to have obtained refugee status from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in March 2025.
She said, the Anjugramam police in Kanniyakumari district had arrested her on December 10, 2025 when she had gone to a resort over there for decorating the venue of a birthday party.
The charge levelled against her was that she had overstayed in India despite the expiry of her tourist visa on May 12, 2022.
The police personnel also found that the petitioner’s Iranian passport had expired on February 17, 2024.

items.title: Ladakh administration asks activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife to stop ‘unauthorised activities’ at their Leh school
points: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, right, with his wife Gitanjali Angmo.
Meanwhile, Mr. Wangchuk extends support to people of Arunachal Pradesh resisting the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project.
“Desert Flower School of the HIAL Ecosystem has commenced functioning of the school without necessary clearance/approval from the competent authority.

The administration asks HIAL to strictly maintain the status quo and avoid causing any prejudice to the case pending before the High Court of J&K and Ladakh,” said a spokesman of the L-G administration.

On September 22, Gitanjali Angmo, wife of Mr. Wangchuk, requested the Deputy Commissioner, Leh, for the issuance of a No Objection Certificate and clearance for the proposed members of the Managing Committee of the school located at Phyang, Leh.
The Administration had cancelled the land allotment to HIAL in August 2025.

“Accordingly, the notice issued by Tehsildar, Leh, has strongly advised HIAL to maintain strict status quo and not undertake any action whatsoever towards the functioning or commencement of activities,” said the L-G order.

items.title: SIT report says charges against KSU activists in Veena George case cannot be sustained
points: The SIT also found that former Health Minister Veena George had not been wrongfully restrained by the protesters.

File photo The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has submitted its final report to the court, stating that the charges levelled against Kerala Students Union (KSU) activists in connection with the alleged attack on former Health Minister Veena George at…
The SIT found that the protesters had not committed the offences alleged in the original chargesheet and stated that waving black flags as a form of protest did not constitute a criminal offence.
The final report was submitted by SIT chief U.
Preman before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court in Kannur.
The charge of attempted murder, which was initially included in the first information report, was subsequently dropped by the first investigation team while filing the chargesheet.
According to the SIT report, the responsibility of the police personnel accompanying Veena George was to prevent the protesters from approaching her.

items.title: Vigilance wing pulls up Kochi Metro Rail Limited over lapses in auctioning commercial spaces
points: Road-Thripunithura phase-one corridor, which resulted in substantial revenue loss over the past few years.

The auctions were conducted outside the scope of the procurement manual, and the basic principles of transparency, competition, fairness and elimination of discretion were not followed in letter and spirit.
Base rates were not fixed on the basis of objective data.
Instead, a trial-and-error method was adopted.
Moreover, e-auction or forward auction through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) was not considered.
The Vigilance wing also took note of the absence of a finance member in the auction committee, in contravention of the provisions of the procurement manual.
In view of these findings, the Vigilance wing recommended that base rates be fixed on the basis of objective data.

It also called for a consistent policy on the auction of spaces for hiring or advertising to avoid the trial-and-error approach to fixing base rates, ambiguity in deciding the mode of auction and confusion over the auction procedure.

points: BJP president Nitin Nabin made a similar charge against Ms. Banerjee during a procession in Kolkata on Monday (November 2, 2026).

On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and BJP leader and former Union Minister Smriti Irani criticised the coming together of the Mamata Banerjee and Congress party.

Mr. Adhikari, who participated in a ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ march at Siliguri in North Bengal, said that the former Chief Minister was not invited to inaugurate a single Durga Puja in Kolkata and that she is going to Delhi to ally with anarchists.

items.title: Mobile phone, power banks seized from Kannur Central Jail
points: A mobile phone and accessories, including two power banks, a charger and three data cables, were seized from Kannur Central Jail during a search by prison officials on Monday.
The prohibited articles were found hidden beneath stone slabs behind the jail’s second block.
The Town police have registered a case and launched an investigation based on a complaint lodged by jail Joint Superintendent A.
The repeated seizure of prohibited articles from within the jail compound has raised concerns over security checks.
Inadequate inspection of food items and cooking materials brought into the prison is suspected to be facilitating the smuggling of such articles.

items.title: Kochi Corporation Council passes SIR resolution amid protests; BJP councillors walk out
points: The resolution expressed solidarity with the nationwide protests by political, youth and student outfits against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The resolution, backed by Left Democratic Front parliamentary party leader V.A.

Sreejith, criticised Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar for allegedly bringing disrepute to a constitutional position through the purported sabotage of the democratic process by stripping over 13 crore voters of their voting rights.
BJP councillors, led by their parliamentary party leader Sudha Dilipkumar, strongly protested the resolution.

BJP councillor Priya Prasanth claimed that over 2.50 crore of the names removed from the rolls belonged to deceased persons and asked whether Ms. Varghese wanted the deceased to be given voting rights.
Shortly thereafter, the BJP councillors walked out of the council hall, accusing the Mayor and UDF councillors of intolerance.

While supporting the resolution, Mr. Sreejith criticised the manner in which the Mayor and UDF councillors had participated in the discussion and repeatedly interrupted Ms. Prasanth while she was speaking.

items.title: Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad seeks reconstitution of government’s health task force
points: Manoj Kumar, general secretary, KSSP, said in a statement here on Tuesday that remarks from those in responsible positions, casting doubts on health systems which had been improved through the expenditure of public funds, only serve to aggravate concerns…
The KSSP functionaries claimed that a majority of its members were heads of corporate hospitals or large private laboratory chains.
It also includes officials known for their pro-privatisation stance.
In the absence of this balance, there was a risk of commercial interests getting priority over the people’s health needs, they said.

The KSSP leaders said that the core question was whether private participation was strengthening the public health system or if it was gradually transferring the system’s operations, assets, and decision-making authority to private interests.

If functions like diagnostic testing, specialised treatments, and hospital management were increasingly entrusted to private agencies, the government’s control over costs, service priorities, and the conditions under which patients receive care may diminish.

items.title: A song or two for the reconstruction of Tagore Centenary Hall in Kozhikode
points: Songs being sung outside the Kozhikode Corporation office on Tuesday as part of a demand for the reconstruction of Tagore Centenary Hall.

Ragesh People who visited the Kozhikode Corporation office or those who strolled through the nearby beach on Tuesday morning were perhaps amused by the songs emerging from a ‘pandal’ outside the gate.

The activists of the Kala Samskarika Samyukta Vedi, a joint forum of over 40 cultural groups in the city, were staging a protest there seeking immediate steps to reconstruct the Tagore Centenary Hall, a prominent venue for cultural performances which was…
“The Town Hall can accommodate only 200-odd people.
Though the renovated Jubilee Hall is comparatively big in size, the daily rent is ₹40,000, and there is no parking space.
The Tagore Hall had a capacity of 1,200 people, and the daily rent was just ₹3,000.

items.title: Ramalinga Reddy flags substandard civic works in HSR Layout, seeks halt
points: Forest Minister and BTM Layout MLA Ramalinga Reddy has written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s Chief Commissioner, flagging substandard civic works in HSR Layout and demanding an immediate halt to the project.

Mr. Reddy referred to the construction of a 1.2-metre-wide stormwater drain on 14th Main Road in HSR Layout Stage 5, ahead of the white-topping works being undertaken by Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited (B-SMILE).
“Due to the poor quality of work, the underground drainage system in the area has been affected.
In addition, smooth traffic movement has also been disrupted due to the poor condition of the road, causing inconvenience to local residents and other commuters,” Mr. Reddy said in the letter.
The Minister noted that during a site inspection, they had observed that the ongoing works were of poor quality.
Mr. Reddy has demanded that the civic authority immediately halt the ongoing works and review the work completed so far.

items.title: State’s responsibility is to equip people for emerging opportunities, not just for current jobs: Sharanprakash Patil
points: Home Minister Priyank Kharge, Minister for Medical Education Sharan Prakash Patil, and Minister for Large and Medium Scale Industries M.
Mr. Patil was speaking at the inaugural session of the Bengaluru Skill Summit 2026.

The three-day event is organised by the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood (SDEL) and hosted by the Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC), in collaboration with the Karnataka Skill Development Authority (KSDA).

Held under the theme ‘Workforce 2030: Scale, Systems, Synergy’, the summit brings together policymakers, industry leaders, employers, educational institutions, skill development organisations, and other stakeholders to discuss the future of workforce…
Patil, Minister for Large and Medium Industries, stated that Karnataka offers a strong industrial ecosystem, investor-friendly policies, and a skilled workforce to support future-ready industries.

Several publications were released at the event, including Karnataka Kaushalya Sampada: The Skill Handbook (2026 Edition), Karnataka Talent Landscape 2026, and Karnataka’s Workforce Blueprint 2030 (Second Edition).

items.title: Recruitment exams: KEA decided to appoint two invigilators for every exam hall
points: A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam. | Photo Credit: K.

MURALI KUMAR Taking into account the irregularities reported at the Shiggaon examination centre of Haveri district in the Village Administrative Officer (VAO) recruitment examination recently, the Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) has decided to…
A candidate in Haveri, who was flagged for poor academic record and emerging as a topper in VAO exam, has now been found to have used a mobile phone during the exam.
To prevent such instances, from now on, two invigilators will be appointed for every examination hall.
One invigilator will stand at the rear of the hall to monitor candidates, while the other will remain at the front.
All candidates must reach the examination centre at least 30 minutes before the examination begins.

items.title: Kochi Corporation clears 30 projects worth ₹1,500 crore for Urban Challenge Fund
points: The UCF seeks to bring about a fundamental shift in the development vision by encouraging urban local bodies to adopt market-based financing mechanisms for urban development.

File photo The Kochi Corporation Council on Tuesday approved a concept note covering 30 projects worth over ₹1,500 crore identified by the civic body for potential funding under the Centre’s Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) as part of its Kochi@2050 vision.
The concept note will initially be forwarded to the State government.
Detailed project reports (DPRs) will be prepared only for projects approved by the government for submission to the Centre.

Under the scheme, which will run from 2026 to 2031, the Union government will provide 25% of the project cost as a grant, with the stipulation that at least 50% of the cost be raised through bonds, bank loans and public-private partnerships (PPPs).

items.title: Local body polls in Andhra: TDP breaches YSRCP’s fortress of Pulivendula after four decades
points: The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has finally breached the YS family fortress in Pulivendula by winning the municipal chairperson seat, after a gap of over four decades.
Jagan Mohan Reddy, with a huge majority of 13,875 votes.
While Ms. Geetha Kumari got 25,434 votes in her favour out of the total 37,992 votes polled, Ms. Prameelamma got 11,559 votes.
Before the elections, TDP candidates were unanimously elected in 20 of the total 40 wards in Pulivendula Municipality.
Of the remaining 20 wards, TDP emerged victorious in 14, while YSRCP, Jana Sena Party and BJP won three, one and two wards respectively.

Earlier, the YSRCP leaders had appealed the Andhra Pradesh High Court to direct the State Election Commissioner (SEC) to conduct re-polling in all wards of Pulivendula and suspend the counting process until repolling.
Meanwhile, cases were filed against 72 leaders of the YSRCP, including Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy and Kadapa MP Y.S.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh makes 360-hour semester internships mandatory for UG students
points: Announcing the initiative on Tuesday, APSCHE Chairman (in-charge) S.
Vijaya Bhaskar Rao said the move was aimed at strengthening industry-academia linkages and improving graduate employability.

The programme was designed in accordance with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, UGC guidelines, the Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergraduate Programmes (CCFUP) and the National Credit Framework (NCrF), he said.
The mandatory internships will be incorporated into the final-year curriculum of three-year and four-year undergraduate programmes.
Non-stipendiary internships will be permitted only when suitable stipend-based opportunities are unavailable.
All undergraduate students must register on the portal (https://iic.apsche.ap.gov.in), which is integrated with DigiLocker to retrieve their Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR) IDs.
Meanwhile, registration of industry and enterprise partners will commence on November 4.

Organisations offering internships to students graduating from State universities and affiliated colleges must register on the IIC portal and complete profile verification before posting opportunities.

Ramesh, and the cancellation of lease to a private individual.

However, since Mr. Ramesh received several complaints pertaining to the misuse of lease conditions, he directed officials to retrieve the land.

items.title: Probe launched into derailment of goods wagons at Jolarpet Railway Station
points: Railway officials said that seven wagons got derailed for around 400 metres, when the train was being moved from a loop line to the main line in the yard near the railway station.
Railway officials said that no untoward incident happened as the route towards Bengaluru, where the derailment occurred, had less traffic movement.
The incident occurred around 7.15 p.m. on November 1.
Railway officials said that the Bengaluru SBC to Jolarpet JTJ MEMU train was short-terminated at Somanayakkanpti Railway Station in Tirupattur.
Senior officials and engineering crews from the Salem and Chennai railway divisions immediately rushed to the spot to restore train services, which resumed around 12.30 a.m. on November 1.
This is the second incident after five wagons of an empty goods train, coming from Chennai port, derailed at Kethandapatti village near Jolarpet Railway Station in November, 2024.

items.title: Minecraft Just Teased the Sift Update with a Mysterious New Block
points: Minecraft fans might have just received their first major teaser for the upcoming Sift dimension.
While the Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 7 introduced several new Calcite building blocks and the Flurry music disc, Mojang also secretly added a mysterious decorative block to the game.
Named the Chiseled Soulshale, featuring the face of a Singer mob from Minecraft Dungeons 2, the block has left players wondering whether it can be connected to the upcoming Sift update.
The Minecraft Chiseled Soulshale is a decorative block with a dull green appearance, resembling the color of Warped Planks.
The Chiseled Soulshale block has a 23% chance of generating as loot inside the chests of the Ancient City.
Although the block is only available through the experimental versions currently, it will soon come to the stable version with the launch of the Minecraft 26.4 winter update.
However, its connection to the Minecraft Dungeons 2 Singer mob and the Minecraft Sift update can not be ignored, and it has sparked interesting theories in the community.

Rajanna on Tuesday, saying he was free to quit the party if he so wished, and accusing him of “betraying the party while being part of it.” This comes against the backdrop of Mr. Rajanna’s son and MLC R.

items.title: Bengaluru: South corporation shuts 63 commercial establishments in residential layouts
points: The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut.

This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation).
According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations.
Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement.
Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed.
The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited.
The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P.
Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others.

items.title: EC: Previously enrolled voters can submit form 6 for inclusion
points: The Election Commission on Tuesday said previously enrolled voters can submit Form 6 for inclusion as electors if their names are missing from draft Special Intensive Revision (SIR) rolls.

The clarification came days after the Supreme Court asked ECI not to make nearly 4.3 million Delhi residents – whose names were removed from the electoral rolls after they could not be found at their last known addresses – reapply as new voters through…
Instead, it suggested that such voters be permitted to restore their names through Form 8, which is intended for address-related changes, or through the enumeration process.

“Therefore, such electors believe that submission of Form 6, in view of their previous enrolment, would amount to making a false declaration and render them liable for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950,” it said.

Falling oil prices briefly eased pressure on bonds, but the move reversed as economic data reinforced growth expectations and uncertainty over future US fiscal policy kept investors cautious.

items.title: TNCCF cancels onion orders, cites poor quality
points: The Tamil Nadu Cooperative Consumer Federation (TNCCF) has clarified that around 400 tonnes of rotten, spoilt onions at the Korukkupet railway goods shed did not belong to it, but to the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India (NAFED).
The TNCCF had cancelled orders issued for 400 tonnes of onions on October 31, 2026, stating that the vegetables did not meet quality criteria, including a radius of minimum 45 mm.
As a price control mechanism, a total of 2,380.32 tonnes of onions were procured in three phases and sold via cooperative supermarkets and 8,914 fair price shops from September 3.
However, as TNCCF officials had found the onions were of poor quality at Maharashtra, they decided to cancel the order.
Around 25% of the onions were rotten, had sprouted or were affected by fungus; and 50% did not meet the requisite size standards.

items.title: Two government-backed startups release sovereign AI models that can run in airgapped environment
points: Two startups backed by the government’s India AI Mission - Soket AI and ZenteiQ - on Tuesday released their sovereign AI models that can work in air-gapped environments, meaning systems fully cut off from the internet and outside networks.
The models were unveiled at a press briefing in New Delhi in the presence of IT Ministry secretary S Krishnan and India AI Mission COO Sudeep Shrivastava.
Soket AI launched EKA-1, a 26.3 billion parameter model built for maths and coding.
It was trained on about 7.5 trillion tokens covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages and English.
ZenteiQ released two open-source models, Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B.
These are multilingual assistants that support English and 10 Indian languages.
It can also run on a mobile phone with at least 6 GB of memory.

items.title: Taco Bell sales fall more than expected on cyclosporiasis outbreak hit
points: Yum Brands faced a setback in the third quarter as Taco Bell reported declining sales, primarily due to a cyclosporiasis outbreak that sparked customer concerns.
While the outbreak severely impacted customer traffic, there was a notable recovery in sales during September and October.
Although same-store sales remained flat, falling short of analysts' predictions, the company surpassed profit expectations, boosting investor trust in Yum Brands.

items.title: Tamil Nadu government releases three-year BESS policy

JOTHI RAMALINGAM The Tamil Nadu government has released a three-year Tamil Nadu Battery Energy Storage Systems Policy 2026, envisaging deployment of 2.5 GW/10 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) during this period.

It will be mandatory for new solar or solar-hybrid renewable energy projects of one MW and above applied on or after the date of notification of the policy or commissioned on or after April 1, 2027 to install BESS capacity of at least 10% of the solar…
Co-located and standalone BESS will be eligible for 100% waiver of applicable transmission and wheeling charges attributable to the eligible BESS, according to the policy.
